title: Best-Rate Claims against a Hotel Reservation
content:
Where the identical room at the identical property on the identical dates is publicly offered for less within the claim window of the rate plan booked in the Hotel Rate Plans range, the difference is settled to the card together with the plan's goodwill amount.

**One settlement per reservation.** A best-rate settlement is raised only when no best-rate settlement has already been raised against the same reservation. The folio of that reservation is the authority: where a best-rate settlement already stands on it, no second settlement is raised, whatever further rate the guest produces.

**How the window is measured and what counts as a comparison.** The window is measured from the moment the reservation was booked, and the comparison is made against a publicly bookable rate in the same currency with the same board basis and the same cancellation terms.

**Plans without the guarantee.** A plan that does not carry the guarantee refuses the claim outright, and no credit is offered in its place.

**What the settlement is raised against.** The settlement is raised against the original room line and never against taxes, the facility fee or the agency service fee.

**After the dates have moved.** A claim raised after the guest has moved the dates is refused, because the reservation compared is no longer the reservation booked.

| The claim | The answer |
| --- | --- |
| Lower public rate, same room, property, dates, currency, board basis and cancellation terms, inside the window, on a plan carrying the guarantee, no settlement yet raised | The difference is settled to the card, with the plan's goodwill amount added |
| A settlement already stands on the reservation | No second settlement is raised |
| The plan does not carry the guarantee | Refused outright, with no credit in its place |
| The dates have since been moved | Refused |
